Sadly, LibreOffice is shit compared to MS Office. Office isn't just a word editor, spreadsheet editor, etc - it is the integration. You can stick a spreadsheet or fully formed document inline in an email. You can see who is on Skype within outlook. You can schedule meetings, appointments, rooms, etc within your organization and with external parties or just for yourself. You can link to spreadsheets within documents, you can have globally or partially shared contacts, you can get seemless email, text, and log based notifications, if you factor in Visual Studio (also the best in it's class [IDEs]) and SQL Server (also the best when you factor in Analysis Services and Reporting Services) nothing else even comes close to matching it.

LibreOffice, like most open source products, is a great start, but it is not only unfinished, but fundamentally crippled by The Unix Philosophy of "do one thing, do it well." For servers doing 1 thing is a great concept which is very stable. For users doing one thing is just a dumb philosophy people try to apply. This extends from Windows vs <pick your favorite *nix> where simple things like unplugging a USB drive at the wrong time can either shit your system or require command line interaction to be able to read from it again, to exceedingly long boot cycles after a power failure due to improperly dismounted devices - all the way into the realm of Office and SQL Server as described in the last paragraph.

Add into this the fact that Visual Studio is hands-down the best IDE available for development (nevermind the newer versions upload your source to the cloud, require always-online account authentication, lock down many of the functions, etc) and you end up with most corporate software being written for Windows. Someone will probably pick at this point specifically, so the reasons Visual Studio beats everything else available (though some other IDEs come close) are:

  • Seamless source control integration.

  • Code completion (you can write easily 40%-90% of your software by hitting space, tab, or enter at the right time depending on the complexity of the software, that's how intelligent the auto-complete is.)

  • Intellisense (similar to the last point, but not quite.)

  • Plugins like ReSharper which have been added in (this is indescribable, there is no comparison with other IDEs or plugins save for the most basic of features which JetBrains added into their Java and node.js IDEs.)

  • Testing - it has actual unit test frameworks which integrate with source control and the IDE and do code coverage and such - nothing else comes close without a separate standalone server dedicated to testing, and then it still doesn't match the functionality.

  • The interface isn't a fucking config file for things like the compiler, linker, etc (this is important because it keeps you from having to learn the compiler, linker, and all the things unrelated to your code to write a program, on *nix it's not uncommon to spend weeks or months (sometimes on multiple occasions) dicking around with the build environment for something that is a problem so little in Visual Studio you have to Google it maybe once every 2-3 years and it comes down to checking a box somewhere, where the total time to resolve is under 2 minutes inclusive of page load time.

The list could go on for all the products described, but the TL;DR: is:

integrated monolithic architectures are superior and FOSS is mostly incomplete, even when it's good*
